approval_source.question_set: Whether the validator recovery drill (T9) and then the R03 floods run on dytallix-staging-3

reason: dytallix-staging-3 was installed on 11 November under P01_T06_STAGING_3_INSTALL_2026-11-11, with the signing guard and the start gate (#134), the startup and readiness fixes (#135 to #138) and the untracked public listeners (#140). On dytallix-staging-2 the drill ended in the double sign of 10 November and the request flood failed in CI on the connection-tracking table. Both now run again on the new chain, by the amended procedure.

decisions.question: Whether the validator recovery drill runs on dytallix-staging-3 now
decisions.rule:
One run of the drill on dytallix-staging-3, as P01_T06_VALIDATOR_RECOVERY_STAGING_2026-11-06 ran it on dytallix-staging-2, by the procedure as amended after the double sign:
- Snapshot: the staging validator is snapshotted first and seen available. The snapshot is kept.
- Fence: the provider reinstalls the staging validator on the same server and address. Delete and rebuild protection are lifted for the reinstall and turned back on.
- Halt, set aside and install: H is read twice. The sentry's consensus log is moved aside at its console, never deleted. The replacement is installed over SSH while port 22 is still open.
- Signing guard: host_install.py guard H on the replacement before anything starts it, then marked guarded.
- Start gate: the sentry starts first. The validator starts only after recovery.py hold prints GO.
- After the first block, the agent is installed again with its command sequence carried. host_install.py verify runs, and finish writes the evidence.
Any STOP or FAIL halts the run, and it is reported before anything else is done.

decisions.question: Whether the R03 floods run on dytallix-staging-3
decisions.rule: Once the drill has passed, the R03 transaction and request flood campaign runs on dytallix-staging-3 under the flood rules already approved (P01_T04_FLOODS_2026-11-09) and the machine rules of P01_T06_R03_LOAD_MACHINES_RUN_2026-11-10. The results are reported.

decisions.question: When the R03 floods run, on how many load machines, and at what cost (asked after the drill passed)
decisions.rule:
11 November 2026, after the drill passed, once the no-cost preparation is done (the wallet fleet made, and funding and priming tried with no load machine up):
- 7 new load machines, made by load_machines.py up --count 7 --hours 4: the cheapest x86 type in nbg1, fsn1 and sin, never hel1. At 0.012 to 0.0144 EUR an hour each, about 0.40 EUR at most.
- The watchdog deletes them at 4 hours, whatever else happens. down deletes them when the run ends, and load_machines.py check must show nothing left.
- 10 transaction floods, then 10 request floods, against the dytallix-staging-3 sentry.
This is the request floods' own window, which P01_T06_R03_WINDOW_TODAY_2026-11-10 left open.

accepted_risks: dytallix-staging-3 is young, so the slow application open at a large height from 10 November is not exercised again. The drill exercises the signing guard and the start gate. The startup bound at a large height is still an open item from the incident.
The staging chain makes no blocks from the fence until the replacement signs again, and the staging monitors alert meanwhile.
The snapshot holds the old validator's sealed staging keys. They are staging rehearsal identities only, and the snapshot stays in the founder's provider account.
does_not_authorize: a reinstall of the sentry or of any other host
a second run of the drill
the floods before the drill has passed
any agent command beyond the allowlist
